chapters.title_en: When the help and the victory come

claims.statement_en: The surah speaks of the time when the help of God and the victory come.
The one addressed will see people entering God's religion in crowds.
He is told to glorify his Lord with praise and to ask His forgiveness, for He is ever accepting of repentance.

chapters.summary_md: The surah speaks of the time when the help of God and the victory come, and the one addressed sees people entering God's religion in crowds [c1][c2]. He is told to glorify his Lord with praise and to ask His forgiveness, for He is ever accepting of repentance [c3].
chapters.body_md:
The surah speaks of the time when the help of God and the victory come [c1]. The one addressed will see people entering God's religion in crowds [c2].

He is told to glorify his Lord with praise and to ask His forgiveness, for He is ever accepting of repentance [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The surah is built as a condition and a result: when the help and the victory come, and people enter in crowds, then glorify and ask forgiveness [c1][c2][c3]. It is stated as something that will come, and does not give the time [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God says that when His help and the victory come, and people enter His religion in crowds [c1][c2]. Then He tells the one addressed to praise his Lord and ask His forgiveness, because He accepts repentance [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the surah answers help and victory with praise and a request for forgiveness [c1][c3]. Another is that it closes on God as one who accepts repentance [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which victory is meant, where, when, or what led to it; the surah names neither the place nor the time.
- Not established: who the people entering in crowds were, or how many.
- Not established: how the surah is related in time to other events, or whether it speaks of one event or of a general promise.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the victory with a particular conquest, and the date and circumstances of the surah. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the circumstances of this surah and on the victory it is linked with. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the particular conquest and its place and date.
The word translated 'victory' (al-fath) is used in other surahs of other events; this draft does not equate them.
